column3: “Most beautiful” makes the highest degree explicit; the second “my beloved” is replaced by “he.”
“His flock” supplies an object not stated in the Hebrew.
“His flock” supplies an object not stated in the Hebrew.
“Each has its twin” replaces all bearing twins; “not one…is lost” replaces none being bereaved.
“Favorite of the mother who bore her” combines the two statements about her mother; “maidens” renders “daughters.”
“Shines” replaces “looks out,” and “stars in procession” replaces the bannered hosts.
“Walnut” specifies the nut tree; “blossoms” replaces the green shoots, and “vines” is plural where the Hebrew has a single vine.
“Before I realized it” connects the two clauses; “royal chariots of my people” attaches the nobility to the chariots rather than to the people.
“Mahanaim” treats “the two camps” as a place name.
